Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28
Start: 14:00 EST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood Product), Sara (Meridian Head of ML), Tom (Meridian CTO), Alicia (Meridian PM)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for making time today; we're going to walk through Redwood's structured output and function-calling demo, show JSON mode, schemas, and the guardrails you can put in place for your product taxonomy work
[00:12] Tom: great, thanks. main ask from us is reliable structured product output for our catalog enrichment pipeline, low-latency for inference at scale, and strong data residency controls
[00:25] Ethan: perfect, we'll demo the API first and then the Console flow and finally Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization that help cost. quick note - some auto-subtitles might say "Redwood Inference Engine" but you might see it spoken as just "Redwood runtime" or sometimes transcribed as "Redwood influence"
[00:40] Alicia: ha yeah we've seen identical sounding stuff before no problem
[00:50] Ethan: alright opening up Postman-like request: here is a text generation call with structured_output: { schema: product_schema_v2, mode: json } - in our API you can attach a JSON schema and Redwood will emit structured JSON; also we support function-calling style where the model returns a call payload that triggers your downstream transformers or tooling
[01:20] Sara: curious, how strict is the enforcement? if schema expects an array of variants but model returns a string - does Redwood coerce or block?
[01:35] Liam: good question - you can configure enforcement level: warn-only, coerce, or strict. in strict mode the response is rejected and we return a parse_error; coerce mode will try to coerce types (string->array by splitting, numeric coercion) and we log the changes; and warn-only will pass through but flag schema mismatches in the Console and the logs
[02:00] Tom: okay and where do those logs go? we need auditability for compliance reasons
[02:08] Ethan: logs show up in the Console and are exportable to your SIEM; for Private deployments we integrate with your KMS and we ship audit logs to your S3 or central logging. we also have SOC 2/ISO notes in the security pack which maya will share
[02:25] Maya: i'll drop the security docs and a short matrix on what is available for VPC/private install, retention, and KMS/HSM integration
[02:35] Alicia: on function calling - can we map model outputs to our existing microservice endpoint? we want to trigger our enrichment lambda that hits the catalog DB
[02:45] Ethan: yes, function-calling can be used in two ways: the model returns a structured function payload which Redwood can forward as a webhook to your endpoint, or you can run a managed transformer in the Redwood runtime that maps fields and does validation before committing to DB. we demoed the webhook flow - here's an example: model returns { "function": "enrich_product", "args": {"sku": "12345", "attributes": [...]}} and Redwood will POST that to your configured URL with retry/backoff and signature headers
[03:18] Sara: nice. and how do we prevent the model from hallucinating fields or inventing SKUs?
[03:26] Ethan: that's where guardrails+schemas and retrieval augmentation come in - we recommend prefixing calls with retrieval hits (your product metadata or canonical SKU list) and using the schema to require certain keys. Optimize also suggests hard constraints: block fields not in allowlist, and we surface divergence metrics in the Console
[03:45] Tom: performance wise, we expect sub-second p95 for single-item enrichment when using dedicated capacity. do you have numbers?
[03:55] Liam: yes on Dedicated we have p95 ~450ms for 512 token response on A100-class nodes with our inference engine when KV cache warm; hosted will vary by region and concurrency. for bulk runs we recommend Redwood Optimize's batching profiles - you can set target latency SLOs and it will suggest batch sizes and quantization to meet cost targets
[04:20] Sara: do we need to change our schema every time the product team adds an attribute?
[04:28] Maya: not necessarily - we support schema versioning and rollouts. you can pin a model to a schema version and do a canary where 5-10% of requests use new schema; Console will show diffs and regression alerts after your eval prompt set runs
[04:45] Alicia: what about nested arrays and typed enums? some of our attributes are nested multi-variant types with enums of limited vocab
[04:55] Ethan: fully supported - JSON schema with enum, pattern, minItems, maxItems. we also offer string normalization helpers (case folding, synonym maps) at the tokenizer layer to reduce mismatch. if the model returns a synonym not in enum, you can configure synonym mapping or strict enforcement
[05:18] Tom: any pitfalls with function-calling and streaming responses? we want streaming for UI snappiness but keep structured output integrity
[05:30] Liam: streaming and structured output are supported - we stream tokens but we also emit a final structured payload. for strict mode we buffer and only send the structured output once validated; for low-latency you can use warn-only streaming and validate post-hoc while showing interim UI state
[05:50] Sara: demo time please
[05:54] Ethan: ok switching to live demo - i'm invoking Redwood API from the Console using a sample schema for "product_enrichment_v1". hits request... [06:10] (typing noises, brief silence)
[06:18] Ethan: result returned: model suggested three variants with normalized color enums and weights, and we mapped feature flags to your taxonomy. watch the Console side panel - it shows the schema validation green check, token cost, and which fields were fetched from retrieval (we mark retrieval hits)
[06:40] Alicia: i see the flag that says "retrieved: canonical_skus.csv" - that'd be our S3 list?
[06:46] Ethan: yep, you can point to S3, a semantic vector DB, or a managed index. we also have connector templates for your data stack
[06:55] Sara: can we run a regression suite against a holdout prompt set? we need to ensure quality doesn't degrade if you change the model or quantization
[07:04] Liam: absolutely - Console has eval sets where you can run diffs across model versions and quantization profiles; Optimize will flag regressions on structured fields and surfaced metrics like schema mismatch rate and field-level accuracy if you provide a gold set
[07:20] Tom: curious about cost. if we run an hourly enrichment job for 50k SKUs a day how does dedicated vs hosted compare?
[07:29] Maya: i'll send a sample pricing calc, but high level: hosted is usage-based and simple; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and better unit economics at scale with reserved GPU pools. Optimize can further reduce token cost via prefix caching and recommended quantization without impacting structured field fidelity much
[07:45] Sara: do you have any reference customers in retail?
[07:49] Maya: yes - a few retail pilots, happy to share anonymized benchmarks and a reference deck - i'll include a one-pager
[07:55] Alicia: what about SSO and RBAC for our team? we have strict access controls
[08:01] Ethan: SSO via SAML/Okta supported, role-based permissions in Console, and audit trails for every model/version/route. for Private on-prem installs you get full network isolation and can configure service accounts with least privilege
[08:16] Tom: okay security looks good. next, the POC - we want to test the enrich flow end-to-end with our microservice as webhook target and a sample of 5k SKUs; also run a benchmark for p95 latency and schema mismatch rate
[08:29] Maya: noted - proposed POC: 2 weeks, reserved Dedicated slot for benchmark windows, Redwood will instrument metrics and share a dashboard; we will run initial invites into your infra for connectivity checks
[08:42] Sara: one ask - can you include an example of strict-mode rejection behavior so our engineers can see error handling?
[08:50] Ethan: yes we'll include sample error payloads and SDK snippets for client-side handling. also include retry semantics and webhook signature verification docs
[09:02] Maya: recap - action items: send pricing + demo repo + security pack, schedule POC kickoff (Jan 6), and Ethan will prepare benchmark checklist. any other items?
[09:12] Alicia: please add a short doc on schema versioning and canary rollouts
[09:16] Maya: will do
[09:20] Tom: thanks everyone, this was super helpful
[09:22] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up - meeting end
